sentences.ko: 아 좀, 그건 진짜 말도 안 되는 핑계다.
sentences.text: Oh, please, that is such a lame excuse.

alts.text: Come on, that's such a weak excuse.
I am sorry, but that is a very poor excuse.

sentences.note: **lame excuse** 는 '핑계 같지도 않은 핑계'라는 뜻으로, 친구가 뻔한 변명을 늘어놓을 때 씁니다. 앞의 **Oh, please** 는 상대 말이 어이없을 때 '아 좀~' 하고 받아치는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이제야 떠난다는 게 실감 나서 좀 울컥한 상태거든. 그러니까 다들 괜히 건드리는 말 하지 마.
sentences.text: Now, it just hit her that she's leaving and she's kind of emotional, so no one say anything to set her off.

alts.text: It finally sank in that she's going, so she's a bit of a mess. Nobody set her off, okay?
She has just realized that she is leaving and she is rather emotional, so please do not say anything that might upset her.

sentences.note: **it just hit her** 는 어떤 사실이 그제야 실감 날 때 씁니다. **set her off** 는 말 한마디로 울음이나 화를 터뜨리게 만든다는 뜻이라, '괜히 건드리지 마' 할 때 딱 맞습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 내가 면접 보던 식당에 하필 우리 사장님이 있었는데 그걸 다 들었어.
sentences.text: Well, my boss was at the same restaurant where I was having my interview and he heard everything.

alts.text: Turns out my boss was eating at the same place as my interview, and he heard the whole thing.
My manager happened to be at the restaurant where I was interviewing, and he heard the entire conversation.

sentences.note: **heard everything** 는 남이 듣지 말았어야 할 말을 다 들어 버렸을 때 짧게 끝맺는 말입니다. 앞의 **Well** 은 곤란한 사정을 꺼내기 전에 숨을 고르는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: I did the windows, I did the floors.

alts.text: Windows, floors, I did it all.
I cleaned the windows, and I also cleaned the floors.

sentences.note: **did the windows** 처럼 do 뒤에 집안일 대상을 붙이면 '그걸 청소했다'는 뜻이 됩니다. 설거지를 do the dishes 라고 하는 것과 같은 쓰임으로, 청소를 다 했다고 내세울 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 거길 왜 찾아볼 생각을 못 했는지 모르겠네.
sentences.text: I don't know why we didn't think to check there.

alts.text: Can't believe we never checked there.
I do not understand why it did not occur to us to look there.

sentences.note: **think to check** 는 '~해 볼 생각을 하다'라는 뜻입니다. 한참 찾던 물건이 뻔한 곳에서 나왔을 때 허탈해하면서 하는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나만 그런가, 요즘 여기 인사가 영 성의 없어진 것 같지 않아?
sentences.text: Is it me or have the greetings gone downhill around here?

alts.text: Am I crazy, or are the hellos around here getting worse?
Perhaps it is just me, but the greetings here seem to have become much less warm.

sentences.note: **Is it me or** 는 '나만 그렇게 느끼나?' 하고 슬쩍 불만을 꺼낼 때 문장 앞에 붙이는 말이에요. **gone downhill** 은 서비스·분위기·실력 같은 것이 '갈수록 별로가 됐다'고 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그리고 이번엔 그 배역 꼭 따낼 것 같아.
sentences.text: And I think I'm definitely going to GET THE PART.

alts.text: I truly believe that I will be cast in the role.

sentences.note: **get the part** 는 오디션을 보고 '배역을 따내다'라는 말로, 면접 끝나고 '붙을 것 같아' 할 때처럼 씁니다. **definitely** 를 넣으면 '이번엔 확실하다'는 자신감이 실려요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그 레시피 알아내려고 이틀을 꼬박 날렸는데, 알고 보니 처음부터 우리 집 찬장에 있었다니 기가 막히네.
sentences.text: I cannot believe that I JUST SPENT THE last two days trying to figure out that recipe and it was my cupboard the whole time.

alts.text: Two whole days on that recipe, and it was in my cupboard all along? Unreal.
It is hard to believe that I spent two entire days working out that recipe when it was in my own cupboard all along.

sentences.note: **figure out** 은 '머리 써서 알아내다'라는 뜻으로 문제·방법·레시피 어디에나 씁니다. **the whole time** 은 '내내, 처음부터 쭉'이라는 뜻이라, 헛수고한 걸 깨달았을 때 허탈하게 붙이기 좋아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그리스에서 그렇게 재밌게 놀다 왔다니 정말 잘됐다.
sentences.text: It's so good that you had such a good time in Greece.

alts.text: Glad Greece was so much fun for you.
I am very pleased to hear that you enjoyed your time in Greece so much.

sentences.note: **had such a good time** 은 여행이나 모임을 다녀온 사람에게 '즐거웠다니' 하고 받아 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요. **It's so good that** 으로 시작하면 '~라니 잘됐다'는 반가운 맞장구가 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends
